title: BWI protests fell short, but airline will still end deportation flights
summary: Maryland activists were unable to get the state to boot Avelo Airlines from BWI, after the low-cost carrier began deportation flights for ICE. But those flights are about to end anyway: Avelo said it is suspending its contract with ICE for financial reasons.
content:
by Josh Kurtz, Maryland Matters January 8, 2026

by Josh Kurtz, Maryland Matters January 8, 2026

Maryland activists were unable to convince Moore administration officials to boot Avelo Airlines from Thurgood Marshall Baltimore Washington International Airport last year after the low-cost carrier began running deportation flights for Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

But those flights are about to end anyway: Avelo this week announced that it was suspending its contract with the federal government and would end its charter flights later this month for immigrants targeted for deportation. The contract was worth an estimated $150 million.

“The program provided short-term benefits but ultimately did not deliver enough consistent and predictable revenue to overcome its operational complexity and costs,” Courtney Goff, an Avelo Airlines spokesperson told AZFamily, an Arizona website that broke the news about the suspension of deportation flights.

The airline’s decision to end the immigration charters was part of a broader financial restructuring that the company unveiled earlier in the week.

Activists in Maryland last summer and fall pressured the state government to end its contract with Avelo at BWI, in protest of the ICE deportation flights taking place across the country and President Donald Trump’s immigration policies more generally. Maryland groups targeting Avelo collected thousands of petition signatures, urging Gov. Wes Moore (D) to cancel the state’s contract with the airline.

Similar protests have been taking place all over the country, in cities where Avelo runs flights.

But the Moore administration, which has criticized Trump’s immigration policies, asserted that the state had no power over any ICE flights out of BWI and did not seek to end its contract with Avelo.

Avelo and Maryland signed a deal in 2022 for the carrier to run a limited number of flights to and from other U.S. cities in and out of BWI, the state-owned airport. The contract enables the state or the airline to walk away with 30 days’ notice.

Even if Maryland had ended its arrangement with Avelo for commercial flights at BWI, that would not have prevented Avelo or other carriers from running detainee flights out of the airport.
